source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Hematochezia localizes the source specifically to the rectum regardless of the client’s hemodynamic status.","B":"Hematochezia usually suggests a lower gastrointestinal source, but a brisk upper gastrointestinal bleed can also present this way.","C":"Hematochezia is more typical of an upper gastrointestinal source than a lower gastrointestinal source.","D":"Hematochezia provides no useful localization information because upper and lower sources are equally likely."}}
source_row.rationale: Hematochezia commonly reflects lower gastrointestinal bleeding, but an upper gastrointestinal source remains possible when bleeding is brisk, particularly when accompanied by hemodynamic instability. The finding should therefore not be treated as an absolute anatomic localizer.
source_row.source_detail: Guideline discussion of hematochezia and evaluation for an upper-GI source when bleeding is brisk or hemodynamic findings suggest it.
